intro: Welcome to Alinda, an ancient city in Aydın province, from the 4th century BC. This is the city where the Carian queen Ada adopted Alexander, and its three-storey market building is among the best preserved commercial structures of antiquity.
history: Ada, queen of Caria, took refuge here after her brother deposed her. Then, in 334 BC, she made a bold move: she adopted Alexander, and in return she got the rule of Caria back. Look around, too, at the city's three-storey market building, among the best preserved commercial structures of antiquity.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the three-storey market and the theatre. Look for the wall towers, and for the aqueduct.
facts: Did you know? Ada's adoption of Alexander was a political device: it gave him the right to rule Caria without conquering it. It happened here, in 334 BC, when the Carian queen Ada adopted Alexander and got the rule of Caria back in return. And the city's three-storey market building is among the best preserved commercial structures of antiquity.
outro: This brings our tour of Alinda to an end. Before you go, a small request: please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. These stones have waited for centuries; let them keep waiting for those who come after you. Enjoy your visit.
